# A ball that contains two balls, two-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_hull_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball that contains the union of two balls, $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$; the empty set and the whole line included:

$$Z \supseteq X \cup Y.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$, $c_y = c_{y0} + c_{y1}$, $c_z = c_{z0} + c_{z1}$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result, the ball $Z$ of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, is a canonical ball.
- $Z$ contains every member of $X$ and every member of $Y$.
- $Z$ is empty exactly when $X$ and $Y$ both are; when $X$ is empty, $Z$ is $Y$ as it is (the same limbs); when $Y$ is empty and $X$ is not, $Z$ is $X$ as it is.
- Not claimed: that $Z$ is the smallest such ball.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_hull_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallHull.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallHull.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_hull_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_hull_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** both balls to intervals, their hull, back to a ball, on two limbs (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_hull_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_hull_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`ball_to_interval_2`](ball_to_interval_2.md), [`interval_hull_2`](interval_hull_2.md), [`interval_to_ball_2`](interval_to_ball_2.md).

```
# A ball with a 2-limb center that contains two such balls (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface",
# "Hull, intersection and split of balls"): ball_hull_1 on the conversions of two limbs, both balls to
# intervals (ball_to_interval_2), the hull of the intervals (interval_hull_2), back to a ball
# (interval_to_ball_2). If X is empty Y is returned as it is, and if Y is empty and X is not, X (the
# same limbs), by the tests of the radii (two empty balls give Y); the selects choose the composition
# when both operands are not empty (qx, qy). The whole
# line gives the whole line through the conversions, and so does a hull whose radius overflows near
# the top of the range. Not claimed: the smallest such ball.

(xl0, xl1, xu0, xu1) = ball_to_interval_2(cx0, cx1, rx)
(yl0, yl1, yu0, yu1) = ball_to_interval_2(cy0, cy1, ry)
(zl0, zl1, zu0, zu1) = interval_hull_2(xl0, xl1, xu0, xu1, yl0, yl1, yu0, yu1)
(c0, c1, r)          = interval_to_ball_2(zl0, zl1, zu0, zu1)
qx                   = eq(rx, rx)
qy                   = eq(ry, ry)
ca0                  = select(qy, c0, cx0)
ca1                  = select(qy, c1, cx1)
ra                   = select(qy, r, rx)
cz0                  = select(qx, ca0, cy0)
cz1                  = select(qx, ca1, cy1)
rz                   = select(qx, ra, ry)
```

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
